{
  "topic": "Perplexity testing of DeepSeek-R1 models with varying expert counts",
  "audience": "local LLM enthusiasts",
  "problem_or_goal": "To understand the impact of varying expert counts on the perplexity scores of DeepSeek-R1 models and compare them with distilled and other models.",
  "context": "An archived Reddit post from January 2024 details a limited perplexity test conducted on DeepSeek-R1 models with different numbers of active experts, as well as some distilled models and other benchmarks like Virtuoso-Medium-v2. The test was performed using a small subset of model blocks and specific settings.",
  "motivation": "This question is worth discussing to explore preliminary observations about model performance under different configurations and to understand potential limitations of perplexity as a benchmark, especially for MoE and chain-of-thought models.",
  "desired_response": "A discussion about the source author's observations regarding perplexity scores with varying expert counts in DeepSeek-R1 models, considering the limitations and potential implications for model evaluation.",
  "speaker_relationship_to_source": "reader of archived source; no claim of personally running reported tests",
  "facts": [
    {
      "id": "F1",
      "text": "The perplexity test was limited to only 8 blocks of the model, which the author states should be taken with a 'massive grain of salt'.",
      "evidence_quote": "This test only ran 8 blocks (out of ~560) so it should be taken with a massive grain of salt.",
      "status": "source-author report, not independently verified measurement"
    },
    {
      "id": "F2",
      "text": "The author suggests that perplexity might not be a fair test for chain-of-thought models because they do not engage in 'thinking' during the test.",
      "evidence_quote": "you also shouldn't compare perplexity here with other unrelated models, perplexity probably isn't a very fair test for chain of thought models since they don't get to do any thinking.",
      "status": "source-author report, not independently verified measurement"
    },
    {
      "id": "F3",
      "text": "Perplexity scores were recorded for DeepSeek-R1 with 8, 16, 6, 4, and 3 experts, showing variations in scores.",
      "evidence_quote": "Experts | PPL\n-|-\n      8 | 3.4155, 4.2311, 3.0817, 2.8601, 2.6933, 2.5792, 2.5123, 2.5239\n     16 | 3.5350, 4.3594, 3.0307, 2.8619, 2.7227, 2.6664, 2.6288, 2.6568\n      6 | 3.4227, 4.2400, 3.1610, 2.9933, 2.8307, 2.7110, 2.6253, 2.6488\n      4 | 3.5790, 4.5984, 3.5135, 3.4490, 3.2952, 3.2563, 3.1883, 3.2978\n      3 | 3.9209, 4.9318, 4.0944, 4.2450, 4.2071, 4.3095, 4.3150, 4.6082",
      "status": "source-author report, not independently verified measurement"
    },
    {
      "id": "F4",
      "text": "The Virtuoso-Medium-v2 (32B model) showed perplexity scores that ended up between the full DeepSeek-R1 with 3 and 4 experts.",
      "evidence_quote": "The Virtuoso Medium V2 distill looks pretty strong, ending up between full DS R1 with 3 and 4 experts.",
      "status": "source-author report, not independently verified measurement"
    },
    {
      "id": "F5",
      "text": "The author notes that the full DeepSeek-R1 model, even with aggressive quantization, appears to outperform normal distilled models until the expert count is limited to 2.",
      "evidence_quote": "the full DS model even with very aggressive quantization seems to beat the normal distills until you limit it to 2 experts.",
      "status": "source-author report, not independently verified measurement"
    },
    {
      "id": "F6",
      "text": "The perplexity test was run with a block size of 512.",
      "evidence_quote": "Perplexity test run with block size 512.",
      "status": "source-author report, not independently verified measurement"
    },
    {
      "id": "F7",
      "text": "The author experienced NaN (Not a Number) results when attempting to generate perplexity with 10 and 12 experts.",
      "evidence_quote": "I tried with 10 and 12 experts and generating perplexity failed with NaNs.",
      "status": "source-author report, not independently verified measurement"
    }
  ],
  "allowed_claims": [
    "The source author conducted a perplexity test on DeepSeek-R1 models.",
    "The test involved varying the number of experts used.",
    "Perplexity scores were compared between different configurations and models.",
    "The author noted limitations of the test and perplexity as a metric.",
    "Specific perplexity values were reported for different expert counts and models."
  ],
  "forbidden_claims": [
    "The test was a definitive or scientific measurement of model performance.",
    "The results represent optimal configurations for any of the tested models.",
    "The author personally experienced issues with specific hardware or software versions beyond what is stated.",
    "The perplexity scores are universally applicable to all use cases of these models.",
    "The author claims to have successfully fixed any issues or achieved specific performance targets."
  ],
  "essential_limitations": [
    "The test only used 8 blocks of the model.",
    "The test is not considered scientific by the author.",
    "Perplexity may not be suitable for chain-of-thought models.",
    "Results should not be directly compared with unrelated models.",
    "The test was limited to a specific block size (512)."
  ],
  "missing_information": [
    "The exact hardware used for the test.",
    "The specific version of llama.cpp or other tools used.",
    "The full model architecture details for all tested models.",
    "The specific dataset used for the perplexity calculation.",
    "Details on the 'aggressive quantization' mentioned for the full DS model.",
    "The reason for NaN results with 10 and 12 experts."
  ]
}
